title: D. The AND, The OR, and The XOR

legend: In the lawless lands of the Binary West, three legendary figures govern the fate of numbers: The AND, The OR, and The XOR.

The AND is strict, seeking only the common ground among a group. The OR is greedy, claiming every bit of influence it can find. Finally, there is The XOR — the chaotic force that measures the tension between the strictness of The AND and the greed of The OR.

You are given a lineup of n%%ZSMJ0%% outlaws, where ai%%ZSMJ1%% represents the bounty on the head of the i%%ZSMJ2%%-th outlaw. You must choose a posse (subsequence) of at least two outlaws to minimize the tension.

Formally, for a chosen subsequence ai1,ai2,…,aik%%ZSMJ3%% (where 1≤i1<i2<⋯<ik≤n%%ZSMJ4%%), the tension score is defined as: (ai1&ai2&⋯&aik)⊕(ai1|ai2|⋯|aik)%%ZSMJ5%% Here, &%%ZSMJ6%%, |%%ZSMJ7%%, and ⊕%%ZSMJ8%% denote the bitwise AND, OR, and XOR operators, respectively.
Find the minimum possible tension score among all subsequences of size at least 2%%ZSMJ9%%.
input: The first line contains a single integer t%%ZSMJ10%% (1≤t≤104%%ZSMJ11%%) — the number of test cases.
The first line of each test case contains an integer n%%ZSMJ12%% (2≤n≤3⋅105%%ZSMJ13%%) — the number of outlaws.
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ14%% integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ15%% (0≤ai≤109%%ZSMJ16%%) — the bounties on the heads of the outlaws.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n%%ZSMJ17%% over all test cases does not exceed 3⋅105%%ZSMJ18%%.
output: For each test case, output a single integer — the minimum possible tension score among all subsequences of size at least 2%%ZSMJ19%%.
